title: Galactic Historian: the founding powers, Colonia, the great mysteries, the Missing and the Thargoid wars
scope: GKI-07 Historian collection: Sol, Achenar and Alioth with the three superpowers, their founders, the Battle of Achenar and the Nine Martyrs attack; Colonia, Jaques Station, Jaques, the Colonia Council and the station's 3302 voyage and rediscovery; the Dark Wheel, Raxxla, the Formidine Rift mystery, Project Dynasty and the Zurara. GKI-08 adds the capital starports struck in the Nine Martyrs attack and their documented namesakes (Li Qing Jao and the hyperdrive's inventor), Lave Station and the Galactic Cooperative, two real-world memorial names, six more lost generation ships, and the Second Thargoid War: the first Thargoid wreck, the Pleiades starport attacks, Aegis, Salvation and three Titan graveyards.
game_version: Lore records are not tied to a game version. Identifiers were read from EDSM on 2026-10-31 and, for GKI-08 records, on 2026-11-02. Wartime and post-war statements (Thargoid presence, graveyard conditions) are as of the cited revisions.
rights_basis: Original OmniCOVAS records of Elite Dangerous game facts and lore: names, dates, identifiers, coordinates, relationships and short factual summaries written in OmniCOVAS's own words. No wiki prose, quotations, images or tables are reproduced; sources are credited per claim.

distribution.basis: GKI-07 content audit (2026-10-31): every record is an original OmniCOVAS statement of game facts or lore, checked with the curator expression check against the cited wiki revisions; identifiers are game identifiers read from EDSM at curation time.

entities.name: Sol
entities.summary: Humanity's home system and capital of the Federation; entry needs a Federal permit.

attributes.significance: Birthplace of humanity and seat of the Federal government, which has met on Mars for centuries.

claims.text: Earth served as the first Federal capital. After the defeat at Achenar the government moved to Olympus Village on Mars, its political centre ever since the 24th century.
Sol was one of the founding parties to the 2242 Federal Accord, which made an Earth government into an interstellar union.
On 11 March 3307 a bomb struck the starport Li Qing Jao; Federal Vice President Brad Mitchell was among those killed.
Entry needs the Sol permit, earned by reaching Petty Officer in the Federal Navy.

entities.name: Achenar
entities.summary: Capital system of the Empire and home of the Emperor; entry needs an Imperial permit.

attributes.significance: Heart of the Empire: settled by Marlin Duval's colonists and held against the first great interstellar war.

claims.text: Colonists under Marlin Duval reached the system and in 2292 founded the Republic of Achenar on the moon now called Capitol.
Capitol, a moon of the sixth planet, is home to the Imperial Palace and to the Senate House.
A Federal fleet invaded in 2324 and was driven out in 2325, a defeat that made the Empire the second superpower.
Capitol's native mudlarks died out after the settlers came. The Federation called it deliberate; the Empire blamed germs the colonists brought. Which is true is not recorded.
Dawes Hub was one of the nine starports bombed on 11 March 3307.
Entry needs the Achenar permit, earned by reaching Squire in the Imperial Navy.

entities.name: Alioth
entities.summary: Capital system of the Alliance, fought over by the Federation and the Empire for centuries; entry needs a permit.

attributes.significance: Where the Alliance of Independent Systems was born in 3230, after its people expelled both older powers.

claims.text: Federal colonists arrived in 2452. The system's mineral wealth drew in the Empire, and for centuries it changed hands amid revolts and occupations.
A rising that began in 3228 pushed Federal and Imperial forces out, and the Alliance was founded here in 3230.
Turner's World hosts the Alliance government, in Garden City.
The starport Donaldson, where the Council of Admirals meets, was bombed on 11 March 3307.
Entry needs the Alioth permit, earned through standing with the Alioth Independents.

entities.name: Federation
entities.summary: The first and biggest of the three superpowers, a representative democracy governed from Mars.

attributes.significance: Humanity's first interstellar government; its defeat at Achenar made room for a rival superpower.

claims.text: It grew out of the government that united Earth after the Third World War, and became interstellar with the Federal Accord of 2242.
Its seat of government later left Earth for Olympus Village, on Mars.

entities.name: Empire
entities.summary: Hereditary monarchy ruled from Capitol in Achenar, second of the three superpowers.

attributes.significance: Born when Henson Duval made his sister's republic a monarchy; victory at Achenar made it a superpower.

claims.text: It began as the Republic of Achenar, which Henson Duval took over after his sister died in 2296 and turned into a hereditary monarchy.
The Imperial Palace is in Capitol, a city on the Achenar world that shares its name.

entities.name: Alliance
entities.summary: Parliamentary union of independent systems, founded in Alioth in 3230.

attributes.significance: The youngest superpower, formed so its members could stay free of both the Federation and the Empire.

claims.text: It was founded in Alioth in 3230, once the system had expelled Federal and Imperial forces; Mic Turner and Meredith Argent were its driving figures.
Councillors from each member system sit in the Alliance Assembly, which chooses the prime minister.

entities.name: Marlin Duval
entities.summary: Led the colonial voyage that settled Achenar, and founded its first republic.

attributes.significance: Her republic became the Empire, and her ideals survive as the movement called Marlinism.

claims.text: A wealthy Federal citizen tired of its conformity, she funded and led a colonial voyage to Achenar and set up a democratic republic there.
A speeder accident in 2296 killed her, her partner and her children, and her brother Henson took control of the colony.
Some say Henson arranged her death to take power. Nobody ever proved it.
Marlinism, which would replace the Emperor with elected senators, outlived her. Its violent offshoot, the Neo-Marlinist Liberation Army, carried out the Nine Martyrs bombings.

entities.name: Henson Duval
entities.summary: Marlin Duval's brother, who turned her republic into an empire and wore its first crown.

attributes.significance: Made the Republic of Achenar a hereditary empire and led it to victory against the Federation.

claims.text: After his sister died in 2296 he used his popularity to seize the government and replaced elected rule with succession by birth.
Crowned first Emperor in 2320, he reigned until he died in 2402.
In 2325 he sent every ship he could find, civilian or military, against the Federal fleet and drove it from Achenar.

entities.name: Mic Turner
entities.summary: Pilot and explorer who co-founded the Alliance with Meredith Argent.

attributes.significance: A hero of Alioth's liberation; the seat of Alliance government is on a world renamed for him.

claims.text: His flying in the Alioth revolt, including taking the gas mining platforms, made him one of its leaders.
To honour his part in freeing Alioth and creating the Alliance, Gordonworld took the name Turner's World.
Test-flying a prototype exploration ship from Pleione in the Pleiades, he jumped out and was never seen again.
His name may nod to the musician Nik Turner; the wiki offers this only as a possibility.

entities.name: Meredith Argent
entities.summary: Scientist and resistance leader who co-founded the Alliance with Mic Turner.

attributes.significance: Co-founder of the Alliance, believed to be its first prime minister; a world in Alioth bears her name.

claims.text: Before 3228 she led one of the resistance cells working on Alioth's gas platforms.
In honour of her part in the liberation, New California became Argent's Claim.
That she was the first prime minister is believed rather than recorded.

entities.name: Battle of Achenar
entities.summary: The Federal attempt to annex Achenar in 2324 and 2325, ending in an Imperial victory.

attributes.significance: Humanity's first large interstellar war and the Federation's first major defeat.

claims.text: A Federal fleet from Beta Hydri reached Achenar in 2324 at the end of a long, thin supply line and was worn down until the Imperial counter-stroke of 2325 sent it home.
The defeat began a cold war between the two powers that lasted until 2381.
Discontent over the defeat led the Federation to move its capital from Earth to Mars.

entities.name: Nine Martyrs attack
entities.summary: Coordinated bombings of nine major starports on 11 March 3307, one in each superpower capital among them.

attributes.significance: Struck the capitals of all three superpowers on one day and ended the Galactic Summit early.

claims.text: The Neo-Marlinist Liberation Army bombed nine starports at once. Among them were Sol's Li Qing Jao, Achenar's Dawes Hub and Alioth's Donaldson.
The bombings fell while leaders met at the Galactic Summit, held in Sirius, which ended early.

entities.name: Colonia
entities.summary: Independent hub of the Colonia Region, some 22,000 light years from Sol.

attributes.significance: An ordinary system until Jaques Station stranded here in 3302; it became the centre of humanity's most distant colony.

claims.text: Nobody paid the system much attention until Jaques Station turned up here in May 3302.
Explorers took up the name Colonia, first offered as a placeholder through the Galactic Mapping Project, and Universal Cartographics adopted it on 25 October 3302.
Colonia Hub on Colonia 2 a, the first permanent settlement, opened on 9 September 3302 as headquarters of the Colonia Council.
It sits about 22,000 light years from Sol, joined to the Core Systems by a chain of inhabited systems built along the way.

entities.name: Jaques Station
entities.summary: Orbis starport in Colonia, the only finished station fitted with engines, owned by the cyborg bartender Jaques.

attributes.significance: The travelling starport whose failed leap to Beagle Point founded the Colonia colony.

claims.text: Unlike every other completed station, it carries engines and can move from system to system.
Jaques gave this Orbis his own name when it replaced Peters Base, the Coriolis he had first owned.
In May 3302, once commanders had supplied the hydrogen fuel, the station leapt for Beagle Point. Its drives failed in hyperspace and it came out in what is now Colonia.
The sources disagree on the day of the jump: two give 19 May 3302, one gives 21 May.
The failure is usually put down to Thargoid sensors smuggled aboard; the station's own history treats that as speculation.
Through July and August 3302 pilots hauled in repair materials until its services were back.
Only this station sells the rare commodity Jaques Quinentian Still.
On the reviewed revision the wiki listed a cooperative called Jaques as the controlling faction. Live faction control is not tracked.

entities.name: Jaques
entities.summary: Centuries-old cyborg bartender and owner of Jaques Station.

attributes.significance: His dream of a station that could roam the galaxy led, by accident, to the founding of Colonia.

claims.text: He owns Jaques Station and makes its announcements himself, in English and French.
After two centuries behind the bar of Peters Base in Facece he owned the station, and he meant to give it engines and go exploring.

Older Elite fiction makes him a conscripted Federal black-ops soldier rebuilt as a cyborg and later held by Imperial captors. The wiki marks this biography as legacy lore, whose standing in current canon is unsettled.
After the 3302 stranding he said the station was unlikely to jump again, and he has remained in Colonia.

entities.name: Commander Cly
entities.summary: The explorer who found the missing Jaques Station.

attributes.significance: Ended the search for the lost station while surveying a nebula far from human space.

claims.text: On 29 June 3302, while surveying the Eol Prou nebula, Cly came upon the stranded station and reported its damage.

entities.name: Colonia Council
entities.summary: Cooperative of Colonia's first settlers that manages the region's infrastructure and immigration.

attributes.significance: The nearest thing the Colonia Region has to a government, founded with its first settlement.

claims.text: It formed on 9 September 3302, the day Colonia Hub opened as its headquarters after a construction drive by independent pilots.
Instead of governing the region it confines itself to building infrastructure and drawing settlers from the Core Systems.
From December 3302 its Colonia Expansion Initiative held monthly appeals that decided which groups could settle new systems.

entities.name: Jaques Station's jump to Beagle Point
entities.summary: The 3302 attempt to send a whole starport across the galaxy, which ended in Colonia instead.

attributes.significance: A failed voyage that, by stranding the station, opened a new region to settlement.

claims.text: Jaques backed a drive for hydrogen fuel in May 3302 and confirmed the jump once it was met.
Cultists tried to sabotage the jump at the last moment, without success.
The leap from Gliese 1269 spanned roughly 21,890 light years, the longest single jump on record for a human vessel.

entities.name: Rediscovery of Jaques Station
entities.summary: The finding of the lost station in Eol Prou RS-T d3-94 on 29 June 3302.

attributes.significance: Turned a feared disaster into the first step of the Colonia colony.

claims.text: Garbled messages thought to come from the station reached outposts in June 3302, but they could not be traced.
Commander Cly located it on 29 June 3302, and within a week a relief convoy had part of it working again.

entities.name: The Dark Wheel
entities.summary: A secretive society of legendary explorers, said to have sought Raxxla since the dawn of interstellar travel.

attributes.significance: The legend behind the search for Raxxla, and a name now carried by a minor faction in Shinrarta Dezhra.

claims.text: Spacer lore says the society accepts only exceptional pilots, by invitation and after a test they never see coming.
Since 3300 a minor faction calling itself the Dark Wheel has been based in Shinrarta Dezhra, offering unusual missions.
The wiki judges that faction more likely an imitator than the society of legend, since independent pilots founded it.
The self-styled journalist Lyta Crane claims the group began in a darkened ring station. Critics say she forges evidence, and no such station has been found.
The name comes from Robert Holdstock's 1980 book and from his novella sold with the original Elite in 1984, which sits outside current canon.

entities.name: Raxxla
entities.summary: A legendary place said to hold a great secret, sought by explorers for centuries.

attributes.significance: The galaxy's most famous unsolved mystery, and the quest the Dark Wheel is said to serve.

claims.text: The old tales agree on little, except that Raxxla is a real place and that it guards a secret.
Its earliest known mention is in a ship mechanic's journal from Tau Ceti around 2296, which already treats the tale as familiar.
Some versions link it to an alien gateway called the Omphalos Rift, but those details matched a children's story and fell out of favour.
Frontier has never confirmed or denied it publicly. The novelist Drew Wagar reports being told by developers that it is in the game.
A theory resting on a remark at a 2020 convention holds that some commander had already passed through its system without noticing.

entities.name: The Formidine Rift mystery
entities.summary: A trail of clues in a sparse region about 10,000 light years from the Core Systems, centred on Project Dynasty.

attributes.significance: An in-game mystery tied to the novel Elite: Reclamation, once suspected of leading to Raxxla.

claims.text: The Formidine Rift earned a name as a place where ships vanished, partly because its stars are so thinly spread that crossing it is hard.
Its story comes from Drew Wagar's novel Elite: Reclamation, and the trail has been in the game since version 1.0.
Some players believed the mystery might lead them to Raxxla.

entities.name: Project Dynasty expeditions
entities.summary: A secret programme of 3270 that sent ships to chart Earth-like worlds far beyond human space.

attributes.significance: Its lost ships, the Zurara among them, lie at the heart of the Formidine Rift mystery.

claims.text: Fearing a Thargoid war would reach human space, its backers looked for Earth-like refuges and left beacons to mark them.
The ships set out for three uncharted regions, the Formidine Rift among them, before frame shift drives existed.
The project was conceived by a secretive circle known as The Club.
To keep the secret, the crews were never meant to come home.

entities.name: The Zurara
entities.summary: Derelict exploration megaship of Project Dynasty, adrift in the Formidine Rift.

attributes.significance: The wreck at the centre of the Formidine Rift mystery.

location.note: In space within this system; the sources give no closer position, so only you can confirm reaching it.

claims.text: Purpose-built for long voyages and fitted with experimental repair units, it was the project's ship bound for the Rift.
Its wreck lies in the Syreadiae JX-F c0 system.
Its survey done, the ship was sabotaged and its crew murdered by brainwashed sleeper agents.

entities.name: Li Qing Jao
entities.summary: Orbis starport orbiting Earth, named for the inventor of the hyperdrive.

attributes.significance: Earth's starport named for the engineer whose hyperdrive opened the galaxy, and the worst hit of the Nine Martyrs bombings.

claims.text: The starport is named after Li Qin Jao, who led the team that invented the hyperdrive.
Of the nine starports bombed on 11 March 3307 it was damaged worst: it alone burned for two weeks, yet it was back in full operation by 1 April 3307.
Federal Vice President Brad Mitchell and several Cabinet members died here; they were attending a government meeting when the bombs went off.
The station's name and the inventor's name differ by one letter (Qing, Qin); the wiki also records Qing as a spelling of the inventor's name.

entities.name: Li Qin Jao
entities.summary: Leader of the 22nd-century engineering team that built the first hyperdrive.

attributes.significance: The hyperdrive let ordinary ships overtake the generation ships and set off the colonisation that built the Core Systems.

claims.text: In the 22nd century Jao headed the engineering team behind humanity's first hyperdrive.
With faster-than-light travel humanity founded its first colony beyond Sol in 2151: Taylor Colony in Tau Ceti.
Conventional ships could now overtake the thousands of generation ships launched since 2097, and none was built afterwards.

entities.name: Dawes Hub
entities.summary: Orbis starport orbiting Capitol, the Imperial capital world in Achenar.

attributes.significance: The starport above the Empire's capital world, bombed in the Nine Martyrs attack.

claims.text: Its parent body is Capitol, the Imperial capital world, which circles the sixth planet of Achenar.
One of the nine starports bombed on 11 March 3307; the fires were out the following week and it was fully working again by 1 April 3307.
In October 3301 a community goal here collected gifts of slaves for the newly crowned Emperor, Arissa Lavigny-Duval, following an Imperial custom; the Achenar permit was lifted while it ran.

entities.name: Donaldson
entities.summary: Orbis starport in Alioth, the Alliance capital system.

attributes.significance: The Alliance capital's starport struck in the Nine Martyrs attack.

location.note: Parent body disputed: the wiki names Turner's World, EDSM names Alioth 4, so none is recorded.

claims.text: One of the nine starports bombed on 11 March 3307; it was back in full operation by 1 April 3307.
Sources disagree on what it orbits: the wiki says Turner's World, the moon that holds the Alliance capital, while EDSM lists Alioth 4.

entities.name: Lave Station
entities.summary: Coriolis starport orbiting Planet Lave, once half of the Galactic Cooperative's capital.

attributes.significance: Where every commander began in the original Elite, and a seat of the Galactic Cooperative's government.

claims.text: The Galactic Cooperative split its capital between Planet Lave and Lave Station once it centralised its government in Lave.
Bombed on 11 March 3307 with eight other starports; it was fully restored by 25 March 3307.
The only seller of the rare commodity Lavian Brandy.
In the original Elite game every commander started here.

entities.name: Galactic Cooperative
entities.summary: Trade-minded superpower of the Old Worlds, founded in 2696 and dissolved in 3174.

attributes.significance: Ruled the Old Worlds from Lave, introduced the Coriolis station and fought the First Thargoid War, which left it too weak to survive.

claims.text: Its charter was ratified in August 2696, uniting Old Worlds colonies around free trade, mutual defence and members' independence.
The Cooperative created the Coriolis station design and spread it.
It helped defend human space in the First Thargoid War, turning trade ships to military work and capturing Thargoid craft that later reached the Alliance.
Exhausted by the war and shaken by a murder and corruption scandal, it shrank to eleven worlds; its charter was rescinded on 19 August 3174.

entities.name: Leonard Nimoy Station
entities.summary: Orbis starport orbiting the planet Vulcan in LHS 3006, renamed as a real-world tribute.

attributes.significance: A station renamed by the game's developers to honour the actor who played Spock.

claims.text: It was originally WCM Transfer Orbital; a Frontier newsletter (#65) announced the new name.
The new name honoured the passing of Leonard Nimoy, the actor who played Spock. It is an out-of-game tribute, not part of the galaxy's own history.

entities.name: Leonard Nimoy
entities.summary: Real-world actor honoured by a station name; not a character in the game's history.

attributes.significance: The real-world namesake of Leonard Nimoy Station.

claims.text: The actor who played Spock in the original Star Trek series; the station rename marked his passing.

entities.name: Memorial: CMDR Garak
entities.summary: Listening post near Jaques Station that remembers an early Colonia pioneer.

attributes.significance: A memorial to a real commander who hauled supplies for the Jaques Station repairs in Colonia's earliest days.

location.note: Documented only as near Jaques Station.

claims.text: Scanning the listening post plays a tribute to CMDR Garak, one of the earliest pilots hauling cargo into the young colony, often with a companion.
Garak was a real player, among the first to join the community goals that repaired Jaques Station after its 3302 misjump; he died some time later.
The tribute remembers him for refusing comforts and almost never paying for fuel, scooping it from stars instead.

entities.name: CMDR Garak
entities.summary: Player commander and early Colonia supplier, remembered by a listening post.

attributes.significance: One of the first commanders to supply Colonia, honoured in game after his death.

claims.text: An early pioneer of Colonia who hauled supplies the long way from the core worlds.

entities.name: Second Thargoid War
entities.summary: War between humanity and the Thargoids from 3303 to 18 December 3310, ending in a human victory.

attributes.significance: Brought the Thargoids back 152 years after the first war, drove the Titans into human space and ended over Earth.

claims.text: Open hostilities began on 26 September 3303, when Interceptors attacked independent pilots without provocation at non-human signal sources.
Eight Maelstroms arrived and their fleets overwhelmed 44 populated systems, with billions killed and billions more fleeing.
The war ended in a human victory when the Titan Cocijo was destroyed on 18 December 3310.
After the war Thargoids still occupy the Pleiades, Witch Head, California and Coalsack nebulae, as of the reviewed revision.
The war article's closing section prints the end year as 3010; its summary and the Titan article give 18 December 3310, which is recorded here.

entities.name: Aegis
entities.summary: Joint research initiative of the three superpowers against the Thargoids, founded in 3303.

attributes.significance: Built humanity's first effective anti-Thargoid weapons and coordinated research and defence through much of the war.
attributes.period: Founded 4 August 3303; shut down January 3308; reformed February 3309

claims.text: Scientists of the Federation, Empire and Alliance founded it on 4 August 3303 to pool their research on the Thargoids.
Its first anti-xeno equipment, an AX missile rack and an AX xeno scanner, arrived on 28 September 3303 and let pilots break an Interceptor's defences for the first time.
After an inquiry into the loss of the Alexandria the superpowers shut it down on 18 January 3308.
It was re-formed on 13 February 3309 under Professor Alba Tesreau, headquartered in Duamta.

entities.name: Salvation
entities.summary: Alias of Caleb Wycherley, a scientist who pursued his own anti-Thargoid weapons.

attributes.significance: Ties the Thargoid wars together: his team worked on INRA's mycoid, and his Proteus Wave of 3308 preceded the Maelstroms.

claims.text: Salvation is Caleb Wycherley, once vice-president of research at Azimuth Biochemicals.
His team worked for INRA as subcontractors on the mycoid bioweapon, and he was present when it was tested.
He was aboard the Bright Sentinel when the Proteus Wave fired; his body was reported found on its bridge on 25 August 3308.
Seo Jin-ae claims he prepared a Nemesis Protocol to keep his mind alive after death; nothing confirms it.

entities.name: Thargoid attacks on Pleiades starports
entities.summary: Medusa Interceptors crippled starports across the Pleiades between 14 December 3303 and 11 January 3304.

attributes.significance: The war's first attacks on starports: the opening day struck Titan's Daughter, The Oracle and Liman Legacy.

claims.text: On 14 December 3303 Thargoids damaged Titan's Daughter in Taygeta, The Oracle and Liman Legacy; the Pilots Federation moved docked pilots' ships to rescue vessels.
Further waves followed on 21 December, 4 January and 11 January, when Obsidian Orbital in Maia was hit.
Security footage showed shutdown fields disabling defences before the reactor was hit; witnesses read this as an attempt to cripple stations rather than destroy them.

entities.name: Delphi
entities.summary: Independent system by the Pleiades, renamed in 3304 and once Aegis Research's base.

attributes.significance: Home of The Oracle and of Aegis's research headquarters, at the heart of the Pleiades front.

claims.text: It was designated Pleiades Sector IR-W d1-55 until 11 December 3304.
Aegis Research was based here, headquartered at Donar's Oak.
Wrecked bulk cruiser megaships lie across the system.
Its name has drawn Raxxla and 'Omphalos' theories; none has produced anything.
It sits at the edge of the Pleiades, where Thargoids remain after the war.

entities.name: The Oracle
entities.summary: Orbis starport orbiting Delphi 5 a, struck on the first day of the Pleiades station attacks.

attributes.significance: One of the first starports the Thargoids crippled, and the first to be restored.

claims.text: Attacked by Thargoids on 14 December 3303.
It was the first station to recover from a Thargoid attack; Obsidian Orbital was the second, on 3 March 3304.
In 3307 a later attack cost it its alignment thrusters and it nearly fell onto Delphi 5 a before engineers stabilised it.

entities.name: Obsidian Orbital
entities.summary: Ocellus starport in Maia, named by public vote and hit by Thargoids in January 3304.

attributes.significance: A community-built Pleiades starport that hosted an Aegis laboratory and survived a Thargoid attack.

claims.text: It was built after a community goal and given its name by public vote.
From 2 December 3303 it was one of 25 Pleiades stations hosting an Aegis laboratory.
Heavily damaged by Thargoids on 11 January 3304; it was fully repaired by 3 March 3304.
The wiki says construction began in the Kaushpoos system yet places the station in Maia; the sources reviewed do not explain the difference.
Since update 2.4 its docking announcements are voiced by CMDR ObsidianAnt.

entities.name: First Thargoid crash site
aliases: Crashed Thargoid Ship, Pleiades Sector AB-W b2-4
entities.summary: Wreck of an ancient Thargoid Interceptor on Pleiades Sector AB-W b2-4 9 a, found in 3302.

attributes.significance: The first Thargoid wreck ever found, and the end of 'the Hunt' that led commanders to it.

location.note: Position as tabled by the wiki, which records Odyssey-era moves for other wrecks but none for this one. Treated as approximate: confirm the site yourself.

claims.text: CMDRs Noctrach and Ihazevich found it on 30 August 3302 by following the last clue of 'the Hunt', set by three commanders.
In October 3303 Aegis's Professor Alba Tesreau confirmed it as a Thargoid Interceptor a little over 100 years old.
The documented surface position predates Odyssey, which moved some other wrecks, so it is not treated as exact.
The Pleiades keeps a Thargoid presence after the war; plan for hostile contact.

entities.name: Titan Taranis graveyard
entities.summary: Wreck of Taranis, the first Thargoid Titan destroyed, in Hyades Sector FB-N b7-6.

attributes.significance: The first Titan humanity destroyed; its drive remains gave pilots the supercruise overcharge drive.

claims.text: The first Titan to arrive, on 29 November 3308, and the first destroyed, on 2 March 3310, after days of attacks on its thermal core.
Its defences failed during a 24-hour meltdown before it exploded; caustic levels kept pilots out for almost two weeks.
Achilles Aerospace finished its supercruise overcharge research with Titan Drive Components from this wreck, selling the SCO drive from April 3310.
Thargoid materials and samples float around dead Titans; the caustic clouds at old graveyards had dissipated by the reviewed revision.
Pilots named the Titans after storm and thunder gods; Taranis is the Celtic god of thunder.

entities.name: Titan Cocijo graveyard
entities.summary: Remains of Cocijo, the last Titan, destroyed over Earth on 18 December 3310.

attributes.significance: The Titan that carried the war to Sol, and whose destruction ended it.

location.note: Recorded as destroyed over Earth; no position closer than the system is documented.

claims.text: The last Titan standing, it turned back into a rogue signal source, crossed to Sol and took up orbit around Earth on 5 December 3310.
Its fleet devastated Sol; the battle cruisers FNS Nero and FNS Erebus and several rescue megaships, Federal Haven among them, were lost.
Pilots retook the occupied systems; Cocijo became vulnerable on 12 December and exploded over Earth on 18 December 3310.

entities.name: Titan Hadad graveyard
entities.summary: Wreck of Hadad, the eighth Titan, destroyed on 26 May 3310 in HIP 30377.

attributes.significance: One of the eight Titans brought down during the Second Thargoid War.

claims.text: Hadad arrived on 15 December 3308 and was destroyed on 26 May 3310.
Named after a storm and rain god of the Canaanite and Mesopotamian religions.
Thargoid materials and samples float around dead Titans; the caustic clouds at old graveyards had dissipated by the reviewed revision.

entities.name: Thargoid invasion of Sol
entities.summary: The Titan Cocijo's invasion of Sol from 5 to 18 December 3310, the last battle of the war.

attributes.significance: The Thargoids reached humanity's home system, and the war ended over Earth.

claims.text: Cocijo's fleet invaded Sol from 5 December 3310; thousands of anti-xeno ships were lost.
The invasion ended when Cocijo was destroyed over Earth on 18 December 3310.

entities.name: Generation Ship Thetis
entities.summary: Lost generation ship recorded in the Nefertem system, found in April 3303.

attributes.significance: One of the Missing: a sub-light colony ark from before the hyperdrive, whose recovered logs tell how its voyage ended.

location.note: Recorded orbiting Nefertem 6 a when found; generation ships can move, so locate it with the FSS.

claims.text: Found on 28 April 3303; the wiki credits CMDR Rhaider.
Its ninth generation began hearing whispers on the comms; the signal, traced to a planet passed 15 light years before, drove passengers to kill until whole decks were lost.
The Full Spectrum System Scanner picks out a generation ship's signal anywhere in its system; listening posts within about 90 light years of Sol carry clues.
Reports in 3309 of a mass psychological disturbance among naval crews in Shamash, with an anomalous signal, suggest the Thetis phenomenon may have recurred.

entities.name: Generation Ship Artemis
entities.summary: Lost generation ship recorded in the Mu Cassiopeia system, found in October 3303.

attributes.significance: One of the Missing: a sub-light colony ark from before the hyperdrive, whose recovered logs tell how its voyage ended.

location.note: Recorded orbiting Mu Cassiopeia C 1 when found; locate it with the FSS.

claims.text: Found on 4 October 3303; the wiki credits CMDR Friend 360.
Its logs show one murderer killing those aboard over time; a smuggled dog was blamed at first, and his last act was to sabotage the reactor.
The Full Spectrum System Scanner picks out a generation ship's signal anywhere in its system; listening posts within about 90 light years of Sol carry clues.

entities.name: Generation Ship Atlas
entities.summary: Lost generation ship recorded in the Charick Drift system, found in May 3303.

attributes.significance: One of the Missing: a sub-light colony ark from before the hyperdrive, whose recovered logs tell how its voyage ended.

location.note: Recorded orbiting the star Charick Drift A when found; locate it with the FSS.

claims.text: Found on 23 May 3303; the wiki credits CMDR Dilliam53.
It could not brake. Chief engineer Tom Edwards stayed aboard to launch the escape pods at the target world while the ship flew past; the captain pledged to name the colony after him.
The Full Spectrum System Scanner picks out a generation ship's signal anywhere in its system; listening posts within about 90 light years of Sol carry clues.

entities.name: Generation Ship Venusian
entities.summary: Lost generation ship recorded in the Kitae system, found in April 3303.

attributes.significance: One of the Missing: a sub-light colony ark from before the hyperdrive, whose recovered logs tell how its voyage ended.

location.note: Recorded about 2,500 ls from the arrival star towards Zephyrus. Generation ships drift, so locate its present signal with the FSS.

claims.text: Found on 26 April 3303; the wiki credits CMDR Klumpozyte.
Pirates boarded it to take the passengers as slaves; a traitorous executive officer showed them a way past the last barricade.
The Full Spectrum System Scanner picks out a generation ship's signal anywhere in its system; listening posts within about 90 light years of Sol carry clues.

entities.name: Generation Ship Hyperion
entities.summary: Lost generation ship recorded in the Lalande 2966 system, found in April 3303.

attributes.significance: One of the Missing: a sub-light colony ark from before the hyperdrive, whose recovered logs tell how its voyage ended.

location.note: Recorded towards Yemaki from the fourth planet; the wiki gives two distances. Use the FSS.

claims.text: Found on 27 April 3303; the wiki credits CMDR Vall.
Passengers came to worship a child named Zachariah, and the ship's air was vented when his followers opened the airlocks.
The Full Spectrum System Scanner picks out a generation ship's signal anywhere in its system; listening posts within about 90 light years of Sol carry clues.
The wiki's location table puts it 7,000 ls from the fourth planet towards Yemaki, while its log summary says 9,500 ls.

entities.name: Generation Ship Odysseus
entities.summary: Lost generation ship recorded in the Ross 859 system, found in April 3303.

attributes.significance: One of the Missing: a sub-light colony ark from before the hyperdrive, whose recovered logs tell how its voyage ended.

location.note: Recorded orbiting Ross 859 B 1 when found; locate it with the FSS.

claims.text: Found on 28 April 3303; the wiki credits CMDR DarkShadowLYNX.
Its council chose to live aboard for good; generations later a disease returned again and again until almost everyone had died, and a survivor left a warning to stay away.
The Full Spectrum System Scanner picks out a generation ship's signal anywhere in its system; listening posts within about 90 light years of Sol carry clues.

requirements.text: Entering Sol needs the Sol permit, earned by reaching Petty Officer in the Federal Navy.
Entering Achenar needs the Achenar permit, earned by reaching Squire in the Imperial Navy.
Entering Alioth needs the Alioth permit, earned through standing with the Alioth Independents.
Delphi lies at the edge of the Pleiades, where Thargoids remain after the war. Expect possible hostile contact.
The wreck is in the Pleiades, which keeps a Thargoid presence. Its position is approximate: search the surface yourself.
Cocijo fell over Earth, inside Sol, which needs the Sol permit.

themes.label: Founding of the superpowers
themes.summary: The capitals of the Federation, the Empire and the Alliance, and the wars and founders behind them.

themes.label: The road to Colonia
themes.summary: Where a travelling starport's failed jump started humanity's most distant colony.

themes.label: The great mysteries
themes.summary: Places tied to the galaxy's unsolved legends: Raxxla, the Dark Wheel and the Formidine Rift.

unsupported.subject: Positions closer than the system
unsupported.reason: No source gives a position for the Zurara closer than its system, and the Dark Wheel's legendary station has never been located.

unsupported.subject: Current control of the capitals and of Jaques Station
unsupported.reason: Faction control changes over time. The Atlas records the documented historical role only; current control is shown solely from the commander's own Journal.

unsupported.subject: Raxxla's location
unsupported.reason: No source documents one, so Raxxla is a mystery record with no location and can never become a destination.

unsupported.subject: Positions of the Titan graveyards
unsupported.reason: Sources give the systems only; Cocijo is described as destroyed over Earth. No closer position is recorded.

unsupported.subject: Namesakes of the other capital starports
unsupported.reason: Reviewed sources give no namesake for Dawes Hub, Donaldson or Lave Station, so none is recorded. Mars High was considered and left out: the wiki and EDSM disagree on whether it orbits Mars or Earth, and no source gives its history.

unsupported.subject: Thargoid materials at Titan graveyards
unsupported.reason: The sources list what floats there, but the Journal symbols of these xeno materials are not verified in this project, so they are not linked to acquisition planning.
